chapter: England, later career and closing thoughts
title: Her South American fan Emilio
summary: A Brazilian poet and director who has all her records befriended her when his group visited, and urges her to tour South America.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But I still feel that there is a market for the things that I do, and I'm very grateful that I still get letters from people out of the country, and incidentally I must tell you about -- I must say this, and then we'll close. I had a friend from South America. I don't know if I mentioned this to you sooner, about the young man from South America that was here, or did I? Do you recall?
Off the tape. You merely mentioned on the tape that someone from South America had asked you a question the other day. But you didn't really talk about it.

Well, I'm going to say this briefly. Well, this young fellow is a poet and he's a director and he's -- well, he's into music. He played guitar at one time. And his name is Emilio Bele de Cavajo, and he is quite busy, from South America. He's in Rio de Janeiro. And he was here with a show. Let me see, that's been about four years ago, I guess. They were appearing at Madison Square Garden in New York, then they came here to UCLA, and he called me from New York. He wanted to know if I was going to be in Los Angeles when they came here, and I said yes. And he said, 'Well, I must meet you. I have your records, I have all of your records, and I want to see if I can find some of your records.' And he said, 'I've had your records ever since they first came to South America.' And he had my album and he had some of the Capitol things, too.

So, when they did come here, and I got to meet him and the whole group, and he was the only one in the whole group that spoke English. I couldn't even understand the rest of them, but somehow they understood my music. And they told me that, some of them said they learned some of the English language through my records. I don't know how.
Well, that's what they said. But anyway, he's been a very dear friend to me, and I hear from him.

As a matter of fact I got a letter from him today, and he's quite busy, and he's into the record bit, and he's into producing, he's into writing and poetry, and whatever, but he's quite a guy, in Rio de Janeiro, but I'm very grateful to have him as a friend and somebody who is interested in my work. And he tells me, "You've got to come to South America. You've got to come." And someday I would love to go.
It sounds like you've got all the ingredients for a good international tour.

Well, I would love to go to South America, I really would, because judging from what this guy says and some of his friends, when they come over here he tells them, "Be sure and call Nellie." He gives them my number and they call me and they tell me, "Emilio says to be sure and tell you hello and give you his love." And they're beautiful people. They are very dedicated people too. Very -- you know, there's no phoniness about them, that's the thing that I like, and when they enjoy and appreciate something, they really like it. And it's amazing, as I say, how many people in other countries dig what's happening here with us, and particularly with jazz, you know.
